reviews.title: Privacy, upload limit, ads
reviews.text:
Privacy: just check their website for businesses to see who the actual customer is.

Upload limit: grandma visiting and wants to upload a good number of photos? You’re out of luck.

Pushes ads to other paid products that interrupt what you’re doing on the app.

reviews.title: Huge disappointment on app uplift
reviews.text:
Been using the app (paid customer for almost 2 years. Recently updated the app which I regret a lot.
1. Picture date is not visible when select photos, I don’t upload everyday and this change is a huge inconvenience.
2. Before updated, we selected pictures, the app loaded them, we added description and clicked upload that’s it! Now the app takes ages to “prepare” the media, it then pends somewhere else, I didn’t know if it has been uploaded as it’s not visible. 
3. Finally you managed to “upload”, you’re required to click on individual photo to tag and mark description. Before that it was a one pager view which you just scroll to handle multiple photos.

I will move somewhere else once my subscription ends.

reviews.title: App doesn’t work.
reviews.text: It wouldn’t ever let me upload photos and it wouldn’t let me go past that page to even look at anything else on the app

reviews.title: iPad App is Unusable with Keyboards
reviews.text:
Hello! Just checking in to see when landscape mode may be available on the TB iPad app. I would really like to use my iPad Pro keyboard. Thanks!

Still waiting on landscape mode on iPad, and it would be nice to be able to scroll faster when adding photos many months in the past.

reviews.title: My how the mighty have fallen
reviews.text: In the most recent upgrade they removed picture captions from the upload page (which means you have to add them after you upload) and removed the dates from your pictures so when you’re uploading you can’t tell what day your picture was taken. It’s made the app so cumbersome I’m considering canceling my subscription. I hope they will fix this soon because I’ve loved Tiny Beans for the past 8 years!

reviews.title: Obsessive Notifications!
reviews.text: Love the app, hate that the company sends constant notifications asking for pictures to be uploaded. No one wants emails every day!

reviews.title: New update sucks
reviews.text: The new update sucks. I can’t tell what date i took the most recent pics i want to upload until after i choose them.

reviews.title: New update stinks
reviews.text: New update is awful. So hard to navigate. Did anyone QA this at all?

reviews.title: New GUI
reviews.text: The newest GUI removed the ability to see the date of the pics when uploading, captions must be made with very small pictures (hard to see which was which), and the upload button seems to have disappeared unless you do this silly dance of canceling and uploading again.  Please take it back a revision for ease in use.

reviews.title: Not impressed so far
reviews.text: This app is very frustrating to use by grandparents, who are already not necessarily adept at apps on phones and other devices. I do not want to see adds and it is constantly showing them, but the only way around seeing them is to buy a subscription. And if you are just trying follow your new grandchild, I don’t think requiring a $75 subscription to avoid ads is a viable solution, at least not in our budget. It’s great for the company though! That is why I am giving this app two stars.

reviews.title: Expensive and glitchy, horrible app, greedy!!!!
reviews.text: They want $75 a year when it used to be free. I HATE them with a passion. Everything that used to be great SUCKS now and this is one of those things. I would never pay for this because the app doesn’t work half the time anyway. It crashes when you’re loading a bunch of photos at once and it’s a huge waste of time.

reviews.title: Glorified safari skin
reviews.text:
It’s no secret most apps are basically modded browsers. TinyBeans implementation is about as lazily average as you can get. Like when you click on support it brings you to their site support pages, but then you aren’t logged in and so the authentication loop begins. Also, if tinybeans is emailing my family and friends every week with images of my kids referenced from their server, it ain’t secure - anyone can see the photos. Finally - and this was the big one for me - when the March 25 newsletter’s lead article is “An Astro Compatibility Chart for Kids & Parents” and they didn’t respond to my repeated inquiries asking if this was an early April fools joke, despite claims that they are a customer responsive company. tinybeans doesn’t deserve my money.

EDIT: three years since I requested and received confirmation that my account and data were deleted, there are still pictures of my kid available on their site.

reviews.title: No longer free
reviews.text:
No notice to my email or on the app it would no longer be free. Log in today and have to pay. So disappointed.

Edit: My MIL paid for a year and repaid when it was up a few months ago and there must have been an upgrade and bumped me down to the free plan out of nowhere when we paid for the year plan. Can I rate below 1 star?

Update -1000 stars as I went to find a specific memory that I downloaded here as my main storage app years ago when my kids were babies and you now have to pay to see your old memories you downloaded when it was free and when my MIL paid for a few years. Insane. I need to pa to get my previous memories back. 🤬😡

reviews.title: Incredibly ANNOYING!
reviews.text: Constant nagging to “add to my Tinybeans” drives me insane! I DON’T HAVE A TINYBEANS OF MY OWN! I just use it to follow others’ kids who live far away!

reviews.title: No support
reviews.text: I paid for a subscription but the app is limiting my posts. I’ve reached out to their “support” twice and received no help.

reviews.title: THIS IS A SCAM
reviews.text: We've been using Tiny Beans for a few years. It is a service that allows us to upload photos of our kids, and it then organizes them by date. It also allows us to share photos with our extended family like a private social media page. We have honestly loved it though it is really just a private facebook page at best. We've had a premium membership for a year or two which was $40 per year. However, they just announced a price hike to $75 per year. Not wanting to pay the higher price, my wife and I decided to cancel. THIS IS WHERE THE FRUSTRATION STARTS. The cancellation page is easy to find, however, when you hit cancel subscription, there is a pop up offer for a discount to get you to stay. The options are "Send me the offer!" or "Cancel Subscription". Neither button works. Frustrated, I look for payment options to try and delete my credit card from the account. No visibility for the card on the account. Even payment history just has XXXX instead of the card number. There isn't even an option to swap to a new card. So I look for a phone number on the page to call. No phone number. No readily available email, though I did eventually dig one up. Our renewal date is in a week, and I have no recourse to stop the payment other than cancelling my credit card. Do not subscribe to Tinybeans! If you do, do it through the Apple App Store or Google Play so that cancellation is streamlined. It was a great service that we have recommended to friends in the past, but now it seems like a sc

reviews.title: Can’t Share??
reviews.text: Been using tiny and for years and we love it for keeping memories of kids.  But I can’t share memories anymore.  When I click on share, a window pops up but it’s blank and I can’t go any further.

reviews.title: Great app till it’s not
reviews.text: I have used this service for 7 years, and every year the quality goes down. Now the free plan is so restrictive that I’m locked out of my account. I tried to upgrade and they happily take the payment but don’t actually give me access to my photos. One year they charged me for the same service twice and balked when I asked for a refund. Great idea, poor execution, questionable business practices. There are better options, at least for now.

reviews.title: Product is useful; business practices are disappointing
reviews.text: The product is fine.  It's not great, it does the bare minimum.  The frustrating part is that the price will increase without any added benefit.  And you receive ads in the app when you open it.  I think I started paying $4.99/month, and now I pay $7.99 and I don't get anything more of value.  And there's an ad that takes over the screen every time I open the application.  I wish they'd have stuck with just having a solid product instead of trying to milk every possible penny from everyone.

reviews.title: Useless
reviews.text: You need to know people’s emails to invite them to view your album. This is the only way?! What is this, 1997???
